transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-20 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (Redwood CSM); Lina Gomez (Head of ML, NorthGate), Marcus Lee (CTO), Samira Noor (Infra Lead), Tom Alvarez (Product)

Summary: Discovery focused on Dedicated capacity: reserved GPUs, isolation requirements, burst strategy and autoscaling, expected throughput and SLOs. Customer has strict data isolation and KMS requirements; primary concern is predictable latency at 99th percentile and cost predictability for billing.
Topics: Dedicated capacity overview, reserved vs burst, VPC/Private deployment considerations, autoscaling policies, quantization and model variants, benchmark plan, compliance (SOC 2 / KMS / audit logs).

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time. quick intro - i'm maya, i'm the AE on your account, and ravi our se is with me, jordan's on for ops follow up.
[00:18] Lina Gomez: hi all, this is lina — i'll kick things off, we own model infra and deployment at northgate. main agenda: we need to understand how dedicated works, what isolation guarantees you provide, and how bursting/scale will affect cost.
[00:32] Ravi Patel: great, thanks lina. high level — redwood dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools, you can pin model versions, and we provide VPC peering or a private control plane for isolation. we also support burst capacity into shared pools for spiky workloads, or you can provision extra reserved nodes for baseline.
[00:48] Marcus Lee: can you clarify the isolation boundary — is customer data ever co-mingled with other tenants in burst scenarios? that's a hard no for us for certain flows.
[01:05] Ravi Patel: so, good question. by default reserved nodes are single-tenant. for bursts we have two options: a) burst into Redwood-managed multitenant nodes but with strict ACLs and memory isolation, b) burst into tenant-isolated spare capacity that we can reserve for you at a premium. we can also set policies so certain routes never burst. there is a tradeoff on cost vs strict isolation.
[01:30] Samira Noor: so for our regulated flows we need guaranteed physical isolation and audit logs for every inference. can you do HSM-backed key management and ensure no KV cache snapshotting to shared storage?
[01:45] Ravi Patel: yes, for private/dedicated we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key material, and KV cache stays in memory per tenant; we persist nothing to shared disks unless you opt into longer-term cache tiers. audit logs and per-request tracing are included in the dedicated package.
[02:03] Tom Alvarez: latency — our SLAs require 95th < 120ms and 99th < 300ms for a 2k token context for core product flows. how does dedicated handle that under load?
[02:18] Ravi Patel: dedicated is tuned for predictable latency; you pick a reserved pool size sized for your p95/p99 needs. our runtime supports continuous batching and can prioritize low-latency queues. when burst is enabled, we route by policy so latency-sensitive routes stay on reserved pools.
[02:35] Lina Gomez: what about quantized model variants — we often use int8 to save GPU memory, does redwood manage model variants for us?
[02:45] Ravi Patel: yes, we can host multiple variants and auto-fallback. our Optimize team recommends quantization profiles by workload; we can store a lighter int8 variant for cost-sensitive routes and a full fp16 for quality-critical flows, switchable by routing policy.
[03:02] Marcus Lee: curious about autoscaling — can you autoscale within a reserved pool or do you only scale by adding more reserved nodes?
[03:14] Ravi Patel: autoscaling within the reserved pool is supported — you can set min/max GPU counts and scale by job or queue. for aggressive spikes, burst can add extra capacity beyond reserved. importantly, we can set cool-down and hysteresis so you don't thrash and incur high cost.
[03:35] Maya Chen: just to call out — many customers do a hybrid: reserved pool for baseline plus limited burst for seasonal spikes, and they set routing rules to protect critical flows.
[03:46] Lina Gomez: ok, cost question — how are bursts billed versus reserved?
[03:52] Maya Chen: reserved is a commitment with monthly/annual tiers, typically lower unit cost. burst is pay-as-you-go higher rate. we also offer committed burst buckets (pre-purchased credits) that give a middle ground. we'll include example SKUs in the follow-up.
[04:10] Samira Noor: network — we need to run everything inside our VPC and terminate at our NLB, plus strict IP allowlisting. can you do that?
[04:20] Ravi Patel: yes, we support VPC-onboarding for dedicated and private: either VPC peering or private control plane with customer-managed networking. we can terminate at your NLB, and we support static egress IPs and SAML/SSO for access.
[04:36] Marcus Lee: what's the onboarding timeline and what infra changes will our team need to make?
[04:42] Jordan Kim: typical onboarding for dedicated is 4-6 weeks: network setup, KMS integration, initial capacity provisioning, and run a smoke benchmark. Private/on-prem can be longer depending on procurement. we'll send a checklist.
[04:58] Tom Alvarez: i wanna dig into benchmarking — ravi, what do you need from us to run a meaningful perf test?
[05:05] Ravi Patel: sample prompt set, token distribution, concurrency profile, and a non-prod dataset or synthetic generator. we'll run a 48-72 hour benchmark on a small reserved config + burst to show p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens.
[05:22] Lina Gomez: we have a mixed mix of short (50-200 tok) and long (up to 2k) flows, and sometimes we call external tools so KV cache warmup is important. can you preserve KV cache across requests for the same session?
[05:36] Ravi Patel: yes, we support per-session KV cache; for dedicated you can tune cache retention. cache stays in-memory on the serving node; if you need persistence across restarts we can provide customer-managed cache tiers but that comes with tradeoffs.
[05:52] Marcus Lee: security/regulatory — SOC2 is table stakes; do you provide logs we can pull into our SIEM and SSO via our identity provider?
[06:02] Maya Chen: yes, SOC 2 Type II reports are available under NDA, we support SAML/SCIM, and audit logs can be shipped to your SIEM (Syslog/CloudWatch/Splunk). we'll attach SOC2 and our security whitepaper.
[06:15] Samira Noor: for encryption, can you support BYOK and integration with our Azure Key Vault / HashiCorp HSM?
[06:24] Ravi Patel: we support KMS integrations including AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and HSM-backed key stores via standard APIs and customer-managed keys for private deployments.
[06:34] Tom Alvarez: do you have any customers in finance/regulated spaces running dedicated?
[06:39] Maya Chen: yes, several banks and payments companies run dedicated/private with VPC and HSM. happy to share references after NDA.
[06:48] Lina Gomez: about fallback — if a node goes down do you failover automatically to another reserved node or to burst? what's the impact on latency?
[06:58] Ravi Patel: we have automatic failover across nodes in the same pool; if capacity is insufficient we'll fall back to pre-configured model variants or burst. failover latency depends on KV cache coldness; we aim to keep p99 SLOs but we surface degradation via tracing and can roll back to smaller models to preserve throughput.
[07:20] Marcus Lee: we need clear runbooks and SLAs — what uptime and support response do you offer for dedicated?
[07:27] Maya Chen: dedicated customers get SLA-backed uptime (typically 99.9% for reserved pools) and a support SLA based on the enterprise tier. we'll include specifics in the contract appendix.
[07:38] Tom Alvarez: one last technical — do you expose metrics for per-token cost, GPU utilization, per-route latency so we can integrate into our cost dashboards?
[07:47] Jordan Kim: yes, console exposes per-route token counts, latency percentiles, GPU utilization, and cost breakdowns. you can also pull via API.
[07:56] lina: ok sounds good, what's the recommended starting config for us? we expect 50 rps with 50% short and 50% long tokens, and expect 100k tokens/day initially but ramp to 1M tokens/day in three months.
[08:12] Ravi Patel: conservative starting point would be 4 A100-class GPUs (or equivalent) in reserved pool with autoscale headroom and a small burst bucket. we'll model p95/p99 given your token mix in the benchmark and adjust. we'll send an example capacity plan with cost projections.
[08:33] Marcus lee: do you support preferential routing by model family — like route critical flows to fp16 model and less-critical to int8?
[08:41] Ravi patel: yes, route policies can be per-path or per-API-key. you can set rules based on latency budget, cost, or user tier.
[08:50] samira: on procurement, we'll need a sample contract, MSA, and data processing addendum. procurement lead will review.
[08:58] maya: we have templates; we'll send MSA + DPA and pricing.
[09:04] Tom: any blockers from your side in running the benchmark?
[09:08] ravi: need the prompt set and network access for test traffic; otherwise we can spin up in our sandbox dedicated pool.
[09:16] lina: timeline — we want a POC in early may, can you support that?
[09:21] maya: yes, we can target week of 5/4 for a short POC benchmark. i'll coordinate scheduling after we send the materials.
[09:29] [Minor cross-talk and background noise]
[09:45] Marcus Lee: (inaudible) — but regarding billing, we need usage attribution in our internal chargeback reports. can you provide per-team API keys and cost centers?
[09:58] Jordan Kim: yes, we support per-api-key cost reporting and tags so you can attribute usage to teams.
[10:07] Lina Gomez: ok recap please?
[10:10] Maya Chen: recap — redwood to send: detailed dedicated pricing SKUs and commitment tiers, SOC2/security pack and onboarding checklist, sample MSA/DPA, and a benchmark plan for the 2-day run. northgate to share: sample prompts, token distribution, network diagrams, KMS vendor info, and procurement timeline. next sync: technical deep-dive Wed 4/22 (proposed).
[10:35] Marcus Lee: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[10:40] Meeting end.
